english: There are two faint paw-prints here- one on each side of the hallway.
I think traps like these are my least favorite part of the job.
So... we trying this again?
(Nod and touch the paw print. Again.)
E-"No. No. No."
He follows your lead.
As you touch the paw prints, the same text appears on the wall.
ENTRAD EN PAR Y PROBAOS.
Enter in pair, blah, blah blah, he mutters.
We actually doing this?
(Get in position.) "Let's go."
Should I touch one of them?
(Press the right paw print.)
(Press the left paw print.)
E-Guess I'll check back on this later.
He gives you a look.
The type of look a father gives his son when he learns about the destruction of the family heirloom - a sword passed on for generations.
It's a trap, Cleric.
It could end poorly, but...
Yes. The only way to find out if they are esoterically aligned or not.
It cannot hurt. It is but the mark that a cat has left upon this wall.
It cannot hurt you.
Just be ready for the worst.
Esoteric bullshit like this has a tendency to do stuff.
You physically cannot reach them both at the same time, no.
You would require twice the arm-length for that.
Maybe if you dislocate your shoulders.
What?
You can't just pop those suckers out of their sockets on demand?!
Should I... actually dislocate my shoulders?
Okay. Sad.
NO.
Yeah. For once, actually listen to your little tummy-ache, okay?
The two walls seem so, so far apart.
Grabbing it, you feel an esoteric tingle down your arm.
But nothing happens.
Not even your full weight - pressing against the stone - could make anything happen.
I feel like it would be very silly behavior to go around touching paw prints in the City Below.
But honestly? Considering the strange traps I've heard of, it wouldn't surprise me if this was some bullshit puzzle.
Bullshit puzzle?
A puzzle? I love those.
...Interesting.
Could be something like...
We have to press both of them at the same time. And that somehow deactivates the trap for a while.
R-"It's worth a try."
E-"Let's not."
Yeah?
This obviously connects to... somewhat close to the sewers.
But who knows? Could be something real neat on the other side.
He shrugs. "This is outside HWBT jurisdiction."
Considering the esoteric bullshit going on down here, it's impossible to tell exactly what's behind here.
But if you're looking to search deeper? This could be the way. Unfortunately.
I suppose.
What's the worst that could happen? Apart from being polymorphed into a Rust Monster, or something.
...That won't happen, will it? (Get into position.)
Being a man means taking risks. Let's do it. (Get into position.)
That would never happen to me. I'm too lucky. (Get into position.)
Oh, no. Of course not, Cleric.
Intense sarcasm.
A defense mechanism.
I heard men live shorter lives than women, on average. Might be why.
This is factual, according to the City Statistics Bureau.
Courage in the face of danger is the sign of true masculinity.
You really shouldn't be down here to begin with...
Or at least fast on your feet.
Wish I had your confidence.
You get into position, and look over to your companion at the left paw.
He reaches up to it after a moment of hesitation.
Ew. Yeah, this is magical.
You see him shiver at the realization.
But nothing more than that, he says and puts his whole weight on it. "Try pressing yours."
Just two fellas, pressing the wall.
Press it with intense masculine power!
(Press the other one.)
Clunk.
The goblin jumps back.
A deep groan from the walls.
That- did it do something? The fuck is that ticking noise?
(Look around.)
An ominous sensation.
Esoterical vibes.
Your body tingles.
A pressure change? Something's happening.
As you peer into the hallway, you see something appear on the wall.
Is that... writing?
At the entrance, a whirling mess of faint light forms a stable shape.
That is cat-speech. You cannot read it.
Ah. This construction must be a remnant of the Whitemane tribe.
This will be dangerous.
What a sexy tongue.
It is some kind of eldritch language. How horrifying.
Why is there cat-speech on the wall?
What? No, that's just- cat-speech?
Uh. Yeah, good question. But...
I can... read this. Kind of.
You can?
Impressive.
(Let him focus.)
Yeah, yeah. Hold on.
Sure, sure.
He stares at the text and mumbles to himself.
It says, 'Enter'. Uh. 'As a pair'?
And... be probed?
Not probed. Proved.
Like the Dwarvish: 'prôv'. It's a trial.
I don't want to be probed...
Not probed. Proved.
No, wait!
He snaps his fingers.
He snaps his fingers. "Yes! That's it!"
It's a test! Enter the hallway in pair, and be tested.
A test? Sounds dangerous.
(Get into position.) "I'm ready."
It does.
We're still going to do it, right?
Maybe we... shouldn't.
He clears his throat. "I mean..."
The goblin shrugs. "Might be stupid."
(Get into position.) "Nah. Fuck it, I'm ready."
(Take a step back.) "Yeah. Let's not."
As you do, the paw prints reappear.
The text from the wall disappears.
Mm.
E-Give him a nod.
What? Are you... The goblin takes a deep breath through clenched fangs.
Yeah, okay. On three.
Two.
One.
Wait- on three or zero?
(Start walking.)
The goblin stops himself from stepping into the hallway in the last second.
I- now!
The two of you step forward.
In hesitant unison.
Trembling.
Stern. Heart beating fast.
The text is changing!
...Stop!
How far are we going to-
Shit, stop!
The text!
You both stop halfway, looking at the magical lettering on the wall.
AL SON DIVINO, LA PUERTA SE ABRIRÁ.
Oh gods, your companion mutters.
Something divine, something... port? Open a gate?
You are too far away to make use of Comprehend Languages. The goblin is your only shot.
You can read it, right?
It's not like I took formal lessons, I've just picked up a few words here and there...
He's sweating. A feeling of dread growing in his heart.
A clicking sound starts to echo out into the hallway.
Tick, tick, tick-tick.
Gods be damned. Okay. Hold on, I got this.
Tick.
All sun dei-vino, that's, a divine song?
Puerta is... door!
Listen to the divine song, and the door will open!
Your doom is near.
(Take a deep breath.) "Okay. Cool."
What the fuck does that mean?! (Shake the goblin.)
Yeah. Very cool.
Please don't shake the goblin.
Calm down! he yells, pushing you off. "Just listen."
He glances around the hallway erratically.
The ticking is... kind of a song.
A rhythm? At least?
He's shaking.
That ticking...
Tick-tick.
A nervous tic. Tic. Tic.
Oh. It's kind of catchy.
Are you supposed to... dance to it?
Dance, eh?
You're clearly supposed to move forward in rhythm with the song.
But without knowing it innately, it would be incredibly difficult to follow it.
Would it, eh?
Figure out what the 'divine song' means.
Follow your instinct.
Ignore the ticking and try to outrun the trap.
Pray to Urth.
Have you read about this?
No. You know little of these cat-folk. Let alone some obscure song in their culture.
Damn it.
The goblin punches you on the arm, hard.
A PLAN. NOW!
Your thoughts scramble as you attempt to recite those words.
Etched into your muscle memory. Yet now, when you need them the most...
I don't have time for this.
Cleric!
Do we- do we run?
Your thoughts focus on divinity.
That unreachable goal, one you will never attain. Since you'll die here.
By fire, in this ancient trap.
(Press a fist against your chest.) "My people, my sons."
...Cleric? Are you praying?!
His tone of voice makes it sound like he's thinking, 'Great. So this is how I die.'
You who trusted in me. I am your keeper, as you are mine. In times of fear we-
You realize, as the ticking enters your body...
It is the same rhythm as the prayer.
What? How? Why?
Who knows?! But never mind reason. It is time to act.
The ticking is the River Chant!
You cannot know this 'song'. It's simply not possible.
Even if it did survive through some obscure document, the chance of you knowing this cat-tune is approximately zero.
But it's not zero?
Unless an esoteric phenomenon happens to strike you - then it is.
Unless...
Yes?
Listen to the ticking. It's simple, but it's also familiar. Somehow.
But that cannot be possible. Unless...
I'm in a bit of a hurry here.
It's been repurposed.
This is a chant. You know it well.
It's the...
It's the River Chant...!
I'm sorry?
The ticking. It's the River Chant. You know it?
The... prayer?! I've heard it, but-
Oh.
He nods. "Okay?! I get it?!"
The goblin has no idea why you're saying what you're saying, but...
He trusts you. Somehow.
He follows either way.
What are we doing?
Follow my lead. (Count down from three, and step forward on zero.)
Tap. Tap. Tick. Tick.
The rhythm lives in your soul.
It must have been passed down.
It lives inside your joints.
The power it wields over you is indescribable.
You've repeated this prayer, this chant, for unity and enlightenment.
For reasoning and meaning.
(Take a step forward alongside Snell.)
One. Two.
Three, four, five.
One, two.
The goblin keeps up. Each step forward made with trembling adrenaline-fueled fear.
Breathing. Fluids coming up. Kept down.
Oh gods, oh gods, oh gods.
(Take those final steps.)
Three. Four...! he mouths as he joins you in those final, final steps.
Three, four, FIVE.
It's just rhythm. Clearly.
Heartbeat. Heartbeat.
Listen to it. You... have to...
...Cleric!
I can do this. (Take a step forward.)
As you do, the ticking stops.
That wasn't on beat.
That wasn't on beat at all.
(Look at your feet. Then to Snell.)
Your companion holds his breath and stares at you.
What...
<shake>What did you just do?!</shake>
Don't think. Just GO!
Wait, what's going on here?
RUN.
You give the goblin a quick glance and a nod.
He returns it, with a stern expression.
(Run.)
You bolt off, the goblin beside you.
Fire erupting behind you.
It feels like an instant and forever at once.
A pressure wave of heat hits you in the side as you pass one of the volcanic holes.
But you escape the worst of the blast, as does Snell.
He even overtakes you, reaching the end of the hallway first. The goblin tumbles onto the floor, tapping his jacket to put out the scorched ends.
As you reach the end alongside him, a final wave of fire hits you.
You burst out of the inferno, out into safety. However...
YOU ARE BURNING.
Your flesh is on fire. Put it out.
(Fall to the floor and roll around.)
Both of you violently smack and roll around the ground, until the fires are no more.
Snell quickly gets up, looking around for more threats.
You give the goblin a quick glance and a panicked stare.
He returns it, yelling, "Go!"
And you completely lose your footing.
You see the goblin overtake you, as you tumble.
Then the fire envelops you.
(Scream.)
(Attempt to curl into a ball.)
Push through the flames.
Your voice is drowned by the roaring inferno.
Your muscles do not listen.
THE PAIN.
As your iron shell burns upon your skin, and the textiles around you catch fire...
(Keep running.)
Step by step, you move through the heat.
Seeing nothing. Blinded by PAIN.
But you make it.
As you get out of the fiery hallway, you see Snell rolling around on the ground, tapping his jacket to put out the scorched ends.
However, he quickly looks up to you, yelling, "Cleric! You're BURNING!"
The goblin helps you put out the flames as you violently roll around the ground.
As soon as you're no longer lit up, the goblin jumps up, looking for other threats.
NO.
THE PAIN IS TOO GREAT.
THIS...
THIS WILL BE YOUR GRAVE.
YOUR ASHEN TOMB.
Oh. Oh shit.
He takes a deep breath. "We're out?"
Oh, gods be good- <shake>we're out</shake>!
The gods favor us, Snell. (Enjoy being out of the fire trap.)
(Pant and groan on the ground to keep yourself from crying.)
We could have died there.
Yeah. I think we should've, honestly, and-
Cleric, look, he mutters and points to the wall once more.
Another line of shifting magical text appears.
PASAD LIBRES, POR MANDATO CELESTIAL.
It says we can pass... liberally? By celestial mandate!
Hells yeah we can!
Liberally? That sounds like... Freestrider bullshit. (Feel terrible.)
Liberally? That sounds like... Azgalist bullshit. (Feel awful.)
Liberally? That sounds like something... I'd support. (Feel like shit.)
Liberally? This isn't the time nor place for politics, Snell. (Feel, apolitically.)
...First of all, every liberty doesn't automatically conflate with Freestriders.
...First of all, no it does not.
...First of all, that's not what this is.
...First of all, I didn't write the text. Just making that clear.
Secondly, I got it wrong. It's 'pass freely', I think.
So I guess we can come and go as we please now.
Hey, are you okay?
Yes. (Lie and get up.)
No. I'm not okay.
Your companion lets out a small laugh. The type of laugh you only get after winning against impossible odds.
Oh. Like, emergency-not-okay, or, short-rest-and-you'll-be-fine-not-okay?
The first. Maybe.
The second. Definitely.
I don't know, Snell. I just ran through fire and/or flames.
(Just get up.)
Only maybe?
Then we're on the same page, I think.
I'd say it was both.
At least it felt like it.
I'll be honest, he mutters, slumping down to the ground a bit further down the hallway.
That was worse than a mass torsion.
(Take a few more steps away from the hallway of doom.)
The goblin's gaze flits around, dancing from tile to tile.
He is looking for more traps.
Oh yeah. He wants to sit down.
Finally, Snell seems to find himself more at ease. He lets out an exasperated sigh.
I need a god damned breather.
Same. (Join him for a short rest.)
Is it safe to stay here?
Get your act together. We don't have time for that.
He looks around. "It's cool."
Considering the fire, I don't think any roaming monsters will lurk this way. So sitting down for ten minutes? Won't be a problem.
He's not trying to convince only you.
He gives you an astonished look.
Your companion is asking for a minute to breathe, after a near death experience.
That is the least you can give him.
Sit. Down.
You cunt.
Oh my. This language...
Your mother would not approve.
You are being pretty cunty right now.
Is he upset?
...Okay. (Join him.)
No. Let's go.
He takes a deep breath, and gets up on his feet.
Okay. Okay. Sure.
Let's run around for hours without a break. Let's risk our lives in the City Below.
You know, I figured it'd be easy to walk around with a cleric? You could just use your powerful magic to solve any issue.
Guess I was wrong. Let's go.
E-Nod.
With a groan, the goblin notices some soot on his jacket. He brushes it off.
This isn't exactly my first trap.
But we usually hire third parties to disable them.
You ever hire any clerics?
So you're saying you're a bit of an expert on this stuff.
You can't even take care of your own territory? You're outsourcing?
Nah. Not during my time.
He chuckles. "You guys aren't exactly available for underground chicanery these days."
Depends on who you compare me to.
Hey, hey.
I'm betting you haven't exactly dealt first-hand with the type of Undercoast horrors that crawl up into a place like this.
Remember that Roper? Undercoast horrors like that crawl up here, all the time.
And you saw yourself, these traps? They're not the type you can just tunnel around, or 'break'.
They're esoteric as fuck.
So yeah. We outsource. It'd be dumb not to.
Rooting around in his pouch, Snell finds a tiny green sphere.
He smacks it against the ground, and it begins to flutter up into the air.
A Sprite-spirit.
Some type of Primal essence.
(Point at the light.) "What kind of glow-globe is that?"
Cool Sprite.
The Nessan-kind. Sadly it's my last one.
Thanks. Sadly it's my last one.
Then the goblin leans back against the dungeon wall - making sure to check for any trap-mechanism beforehand.
Look, I work mainly in Upper and Lower Tolstad. The City Below is not my responsibility. Usually.
So apologies if I don't have these magically shifting tunnels memorized like some veteran adventurer.
Apology accepted.
No need to apologize. From what I've read, the City Below is incredibly dangerous.
And I apologize for not manifesting a divine intervention.
He lets out another sigh. This time in pure exhaustion.
Damn right.
Yeah. You should work on that.
You've heard that the City Below changes from time to time. But most people believe it to be a myth.
The old guard used to deal with the tunnels all the time. But since Urth's death, that work has been entirely relegated to the three goblin tribes.
It's sad we clerics don't get to delve these days. Don't want to leave all the fun to you goblins.
I've never seen a tunnel shift. And I've gone through a fair amount of them.
I thought the 'shifting tunnels-thing' was a myth.
Not sure I'd describe this hellhole as fun.
But just for future reference...
What, like around sewer-level?
Yeah. Something like that.
Mostly above the sewers. The Palace has a ton of them.
That's barely the City Below, Cleric.
I'm not a dungeoneer, but I can promise you: everything at this level and below changes over time.
It's like the city's entire base is an Esoteric Pocket, going all the way down to the Gravity Flip.
It's not.
He states it plainly and quickly, as if he's had to prove it often.
This place... it's real close to the Garden, right?
Sure.
Wasn't here a couple of months ago.
Between the garden and the Waterlane sewers, I'm a hundred percent sure there was a slanted hallway full of frozen spikes. We boarded them up as well as we could at the time.
Tsk. Boarding up. That only lasted a couple hours.
It moved around?
Yeah. It moved around. All of this shit does.
The esoteric madness down here was mostly managed after the conquest.
But it still rises at times. In spurts of violence and esoteric randomness.
The goblin has no proof of his inane theories.
Hallways don't simply move around. Not without powerful Arcanists around.
The esoteric nature of the City Below is well documented.
It has mainly to do with sentience, if you believe the few scholars who have been allowed to investigate it.
The more living minds present, the less chaotic a section will be.
But this, what the goblin describes, that is enough activity to warrant a proper look.
That's insane. I figured all the shifting calmed down after the conquest.
Hm. Can you prove it?
It didn't. Or, I mean...
From what I understand, your dead god and his paladins used to keep things clean.
But nowadays it's getting weirder by the day.
But hey, now you're here, so you can take on this esoteric bullshit, right?
Do well, and I'll buy you a beer. Deal?
Uh. Sure. (Look shifty.)
I don't drink, Snell.
Wait. Right, you... you're not allowed?
I am not, no.
Maybe a little one. A tiny glass? Tiny glass of beer?
He shrugs. "It's not like they have a way to check, right?"
No, they do.
They do?
They scan us.
They scan you?
Detect Poison and Disease. They check us sometimes.
Detect Poison and Disease?!
Sure! You just sit tight here and chill for a couple of weeks. I'll come back and visit you.
If the tunnels are the same, I'll owe you a beer.
We can get back to the 'quest' afterwards.
He is making fun of your dumb request.
I don't want to wait here for weeks. Are you stupid?
I'm not sure how that will prove anything.
Funny.
Oh, shit. I keep forgetting you're like, an actual cleric.
No alcohol at all, eh?
Remember the words. Intoxicants are the work of evil and chaos. As clerics, we must-

Of course not! Intoxicants are the work of evil and chaos. As clerics, we must abstain to maintain our fight against discord. Plus, we cannot cloud our minds. We must remain vigilant, so we can fulfill our sacred quests, and make sound judgments upon our people.
I don't like the taste.
Yeah, yeah. He waves a claw, clearly not listening.
Oh? So you've tried it at least.
You were fourteen years old. They had lax security at the dance clubs in those days.
A shameful past.
Those were the days.
I was a wild kid.
Of course. I'm not a square, Snell.
Wasn't my thing.
I'm sure you were.
Oh, no, of course.
You're practically a circle.
Hm. Yeah, it's not for everyone.
He sighs. "Guess I am."
No, but it'll get me away from dumb questions at least.
Very.
But trust me, the City Below is very esoteric.
Snell is more than correct. The grand power present in these ancient walls has compounded over eras.
All while the mystery of the Pillars - these relics of the Gate War, of Jor - is left as a hole in our collective understanding.
We do not know why the City Below is so esoteric. We cannot know. Not in any sensible manner.
But if you listen - if you feel the vastness by just sitting here, deep inside the Belly of the Whale... then you know all too well the mind-consuming truth.
The City Below City is alive.
ALIVE.
(Nod, somewhat.)
It's also really fucked up. Which explains why your beloved city would give up the property rights to a bunch of goblins, huh?
He laughs.
A sad laugh.
And these last couple of years there's been more and more Reedsian scholars going delving, to study it.
The Old Lady doesn't let them in on her turf, of course. Chasing them away is one of my many jobs - politely, of course. I'm not some syndicate gangster.
He instinctively throws out that gangster comment. Bit of a sensitive topic...
...But the other tribes are more accepting. For a ton of coin, of course.
What is your job, exactly?
Nice work, by the way. With the trap.
So remind me: what's our goal down here?
I've been meaning to ask, but what can you tell me about Lady Sageleaf?
M-"You know..." (Gesture towards him.) "It's good to see this."
I'm a runner. And handler. Of the HWBT.
(Look at him until he actually tells you what he does.)
So you're a sexy rogue, like me!
He lets out a painful groan.
First of all, no. I am not.
Secondly, no you are not.
He crosses his arms.
I do a ton of stuff, okay?
I run errands for the Old Lady, anything she needs. I also make sure our operations run smoothly. Everything from the apartment rentals, to the CBS-
